title: Director, Entrepreneurship Development
description: THE OPPORTUNITY The Director, Entrepreneurship Development is accountable for defining, leading, and executing the Entrepreneurship Development strategy and portfolio for Nigeria, positioning entrepreneurship as a core pathway to dignified and fulfilling work for young women and men. The role is also responsible for cultivating high-trust partnerships and ensuring strong relationship stewardship, as well as operational excellence of the Nigeria entrepreneurship portfolio. The role is also accountable for risk management and fiduciary responsibility, ensuring that resources are used as intended and that portfolio investments comply with Foundation policies and standards. Reporting to the Country Director, the role provides country-level strategic and portfolio leadership for entrepreneurship development, setting the national roadmap, shaping system-level interventions across markets, finance, capacity, and digital solutions, and enabling partners and internal teams to deliver outcomes at scale. The Director operates as a portfolio owner and system enabler, translating Foundation strategy and Board priorities into coherent country investments, strengthening local ecosystem partners, and ensuring the entrepreneurship portfolio delivers measurable results, enterprise growth, and productivity outcomes aligned to the Foundation’s goals. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE 1.Strategy, Portfolio & Delivery Leadership Define and own the Nigeria Entrepreneurship Development strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligned to Foundation enterprise priorities and country employment objectives. Translate strategy into a coherent, investable country portfolio with clear outcomes, performance indicators, and learning priorities. Provide end-to-end leadership of the entrepreneurship portfolio, including prioritization, sequencing, performance management, and course correction. Ensure programs move beyond pilots to scalable models capable of achieving national impact. Embed market systems thinking in program design, addressing root causes of entrepreneurial constraints. Ensure entrepreneurship programming contributes directly to Country Programs priorities and national delivery objectives. Use data, learning, and evidence to inform portfolio decisions, scale effective models, and adapt or discontinue underperforming approaches. 2.Partner Enablement & Ecosystem Leadership Build and steward high-trust, high-impact relationships with ecosystem partners across government, private sector, financial institutions, intermediaries, and support organizations. Enable partners to execute effectively and at scale by setting clear strategic direction, performance expectations, and delivery standards. Strengthen partner institutional and operational capacity to deliver sustainable outcomes. Foster coordination across ecosystem actors to improve coherence and reduce fragmentation. Represent the Foundation in high-level forums, convenings, and ecosystem platforms related to entrepreneurship development in Nigeria. Position the Foundation as a credible thought partner and convener within the entrepreneurship ecosystem. 3. Markets, Access to Finance & Digital Solutions Provide strategic oversight for interventions that expand market access, value-chain participation, and commercial opportunities for young entrepreneurs. Guide access-to-finance and financial inclusion strategies that improve affordability, suitability, and reach of financial services. Integrate technology and digital solutions as core enablers across the entrepreneurship portfolio to improve efficiency, scale, and impact. 4. Financial, Risk & Fiduciary Accountability Maintain oversight of financial stewardship across the entrepreneurship portfolio, ensuring resources are used efficiently and for intended purposes. Proactively identify and manage strategic, operational, and delivery risks. Ensure compliance with Foundation financial, legal, and governance requirements across partners and programs. Maintain strong accountability for partner performance, delivery quality, and value-for-money. 5. Culture, People & Leadership Establish and lead a high-performing, values-driven Entrepreneurship Development function aligned to country priorities and portfolio needs. Build leadership capability, accountability, and a strong culture of performance, learning, and collaboration. WHO YOU ARE Advanced degree in business, economics, finance, entrepreneurship, development studies, or a related field. Relevant professional qualifications: membership of a relevant professional body is an advantage. Minimum of 15 years’ experience leading strategy and complex programs in entrepreneurship, private sector development, or related fields. Previous experience in leading functions, divisions in an organization is and added advantage. At least 8 years in senior leadership roles, with accountability for multi-partner, multi country, multi-year portfolios. Demonstrated experience designing and scaling entrepreneurship or market-oriented initiatives in large complex markets. Deep expertise in at least two entrepreneurship thematic areas: market opportunities, access to finance, capacity development, technology/digital solutions, or financial inclusion. Strong understanding of Nigeria’s enterprise, employment, and innovation landscape. Proven ability to engage credibly with senior leaders across government, private sector, financial institutions, and development ecosystems. Demonstrated experience in building and leading multi-cultural, high-performing teams. Strong systems and market-thinking capability. Proven portfolio governance, performance management, and risk oversight skills. Excellent stakeholder management and influence at senior levels. Strategic communicator able to operate across executive, technical, and partner environments. Ability to lead and enable high-performing, multidisciplinary teams. Results-oriented, innovative, and effective in complex and ambiguous environments. High professional maturity, cultural sensitivity, and integrity aligned with the Foundation’s values. Demonstrated commitment to Mastercard Foundation’s mission and vision. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment. For more information and to sign up for the Foundation’s newsletter, please visit http://www.mastercardfdn.org/ Follow the Foundation on Twitter at MastercardFdn

title: Lead, Entrepreneurship
description: THE OPPORTUNITY The Lead, Entrepreneurship will support the implementation of entrepreneurship-related programs in Kenya, working closely with the Head, Entrepreneurship. This role will apply deep technical expertise in entrepreneurship to help shape, manage, and adapt the Foundations programmatic work, ensuring alignment with the Foundations strategy and the unique context of Kenya. The role will contribute to partnerships that unlock dignified and fulfilling work for young people and support innovations that strengthen the entrepreneurial ecosystem. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Support the development of the country strategy through technical insights on entrepreneurship and employment systems. Manage assigned programs related to entrepreneurship and financial inclusion, particularly those focused on rural and agricultural finance. Support the adaptation and implementation of program strategies to the country context, ensuring responsiveness to local needs and opportunities. Collaborate with implementation partners to ensure effective delivery of program activities, providing technical input where required. Maintain and strengthen relationships with partner organizations and stakeholders to support successful program outcomes. Support the design and execution of initiatives that drive innovation and scale in entrepreneurship. Contribute to learning and evidence-building by capturing lessons learned, documenting success stories, and participating in internal reviews. Share insights and learnings with internal teams and external stakeholders to inform thought leadership on youth employment in Africa. Participate in due diligence and review processes for potential new programs and partnerships. Monitor program performance and report on key metrics and progress toward outcomes. Ensure alignment of programs with the Foundation’s values, principles, and country-level objectives. Support the coordination of internal working groups and cross-functional collaboration related to entrepreneurship. Engage in activities to continuously build subject matter expertise in entrepreneurship and the broader ecosystem. WHO YOU ARE Bachelor’s or Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Finance, Business Minimum 10 years’ experience with MFIs, banks or investment companies operational in Africa to finance SMEs, with special focus on Kenya, with five (5) years of management experience. Deep understanding of the Kenyan entrepreneurship landscape, including rural, agricultural, and informal sectors. Experience working with or managing implementation partners. Demonstrated Knowledge of systems change approaches and an adaptive learning mindset. Excellent analytical skills, the ability to think strategically and contribute as a thought partner in the Foundation’s strategy development. Excellent budgeting skills with the ability to manage a large portfolio of assets. Excellent command of quantitative and qualitative business analytics. Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills with the ability to articulate information to a variety of constituents across cultures. Excellent project management skills, including multi-stakeholder projects. Excellent knowledge of digital inclusion policy is an asset. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment. For more information and to sign up for the Foundation’s newsletter, please visit http://www.mastercardfdn.org/ Follow the Foundation on Twitter at MastercardFdn

title: Head, Entrepreneurship
description: THE OPPORTUNITY This role leads the Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development portfolio in alignment with national priorities and the Foundation’s strategy in Kenya to enable access to dignified and fulfilling work for young people. It drives inclusive entrepreneurship and Access to Finance strategies to support MSMEs (young women-led MSMEs in particular), while overseeing program design, delivery, and performance. The role also supports cross-cutting enterprise efforts, fosters strategic partnerships, and leads a high-performing team to scale impact and opportunity for young people across key sectors. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Lead the design and execution of the Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development portfolio of the country strategy, ensuring alignment with national priorities and the Foundation’s vision. Build out and integrate an inclusive Access to Finance strategy that enhances financial inclusion and MSME growth for youth and women-led enterprises. Define short- and long-term goals for the portfolio, guiding strategic direction, programmatic design, and partnership choices. Oversee the implementation and performance of entrepreneurship-focused programs and partnerships, ensuring effective delivery, coordination, and continuous improvement. Provide support to other strategic pillars on matters access to finance and enterprise development Guide the design and implementation of market-driven interventions in access to finance, digital enablement, BDS, and sectoral entrepreneurship (e.g., agriculture and green economy). Embed technology as an enabler across the portfolio. Manage program risks and develop mitigation strategies to ensure sustainable impact Cultivate and manage strategic relationships with partners, government institutions, and entrepreneurship ecosystems to amplify scale and impact. Foster knowledge exchange and learning through internal and external convenings, documentation of insights, and active participation in communities of practice. Promote innovation, agility, and a results-driven culture to enable impactful partnerships and scalable solutions. Coach, mentor, and empower team members to uphold Foundation values and deliver meaningful outcomes for young people. Provide leadership and performance management for the Entrepreneurship team and contribute to cross-functional team development. Collaborate across countries, functions, and leadership levels to strengthen the Foundation’s entrepreneurship portfolio. WHO YOU ARE Bachelor’s or master’s degree or equivalent in Business Administration, Economics, Entrepreneurship, or related field. Minimum of fifteen 15 years of experience in the Entrepreneurship & Enterprise Development /Business Development or related role in the private sector, with seven (7) years of experience leading and managing a team. Demonstrated expertise and established networks and relationships in Entrepreneurship & Enterprise Development /Business Development or related sector in Kenya. Deep knowledge of the country’s employment, job creation, innovation landscape Proven track record of working with and mentoring successful entrepreneurship endeavors Experience in initiating new initiatives, preferable in Enterprise/Business development Proven experience effectively engaging and collaborating with high-level government officials, key partners, media, business leaders and other network influencers. Experience with entrepreneurship or intrapreneurship. Demonstrated knowledge of Kenyan economic, political context, public sector priorities, and evolving nature of private sector Exposure to systems thinking with an ability to understand and engage with stakeholders in Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development and design programming that addresses root causes and critical needs. Substantive knowledge of key issues and emerging trends and barriers in Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development integration and strong understanding of Country policy, practices, and priorities. Strategic thinker, Innovative with strong influencing skills Ability to interact with diverse and senior stakeholders Demonstrates strong organizational skills with excellent prioritization and attention to detail. Excellent leadership and team management skill Comfortable and highly effective when faced with ambiguity and/or complexity Able to formulate and develop new or creative ideas and approaches The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment.
